info.title: Cross Mesh Ingress API
info.description:
Give your Stellar users an **EVM deposit address for USDC**. USDC sent to it on a supported chain is bridged through Circle's CCTP and delivered to the Stellar account bound to that address.

### Quick start
Authenticate every request with `Authorization: Bearer sk_{key_id}_{secret}`. Create keys in the [console](https://ingress-testnet.crossmesh.xyz/).

1. **Get the address.** Call `POST /v1/deposit-addresses` with the user's Stellar address, `delivery_asset`: `"USDC"`, or `"XLM"` for XLM (see *XLM delivery*), and `speed`: `"standard"`, or `"fast"` for Circle's fast transfers (see *Transfer speeds*). In your app each recipient has exactly one deposit address per delivery asset and speed, permanently, so call it whenever you display the address.
2. **Verify it** before you show it to the user (see *Verifying an address*).
3. **The user sends USDC** to it on a chain that `GET /v1/chains` lists as `active` (see *What to send*).
4. **Deposits appear automatically** a few blocks later in `GET /v1/deposits?recipient=…`. Each one moves from `confirmed` to `settling` to `completed`.
5. **Show what arrived** with `GET /v1/settlements/{settlement_id}`, using the deposit's `settlement_id`. Its `delivery` is the asset and amount the recipient received on Stellar, and `fees` what was charged.

### Concepts
- **Deposit address:** an EVM address bound to one Stellar recipient, one delivery asset and one transfer speed. The same address works on every supported chain and is never replaced.
- **Delivery asset:** what the recipient receives, chosen per address with `delivery_asset`: `USDC`, or `XLM` where XLM delivery is offered (see *XLM delivery*).
- **Deposit:** one incoming USDC transfer to a deposit address.
- **Amounts:** every amount, fees included, is a string of base units, and the `decimals` in the same object gives its decimal places: `"1100000"` with `decimals` 6 is 1.10 USDC. Every amount is USDC (6 decimals) today; read `decimals` rather than assuming 6. The one exception is `fee_rate_ppm`, a rate in parts per million, not an amount.
- **Settlement:** one delivery to the recipient. We move the address's whole balance on one chain in one EVM transaction, which arrives as one credit on Stellar. Deposits that arrive close together are delivered together, and fees are charged per settlement, not per deposit.

### Trustless by design
We never hold user funds. A deposit address is not a wallet we have a key for. It is the address of a small smart contract (a CREATE2 *forwarder*) with the Stellar recipient written into the address itself, so USDC sent there can only be settled to that recipient, through Circle's CCTP. No key, admin or upgrade can redirect it.

- **We cannot send funds anywhere else.** Our operator key can only start a settlement to the committed recipient and pay its gas. Even a stolen key cannot redirect funds.
- **Funds cannot get stuck with us.** If we ever stop operating, anyone can move an address's USDC to its recipient, without us and without fees (see *Self-rescue*).
- **You can check every address.** Each one is computed from public, immutable contracts (see *Verifying an address*).

The forwarder, factory and config contracts are open source: [github.com/lightsail-network/crossmesh-ingress-contracts](https://github.com/lightsail-network/crossmesh-ingress-contracts/).

### XLM delivery
With `delivery_asset: "XLM"` the recipient receives **XLM** instead of USDC. A Stellar account cannot receive anything until it holds XLM, and an XLM payment creates the account if it does not exist yet, so this onboards new users: the recipient needs neither an account nor a trustline beforehand. `xlm_delivery` in `GET /v1/chains` says whether XLM delivery is offered and `active` in this environment.

- **The vault.** An XLM address commits the recipient's **vault** instead of the recipient: a small Stellar contract at an address our VaultFactory derives from the recipient. The USDC is minted into the vault, and we then convert it to XLM, which is paid to the recipient in the same transaction. What reaches a vault can only go to its recipient: as XLM through the conversion, or as the USDC itself if the recipient withdraws it.
- **The price.** We convert through a decentralized exchange on Stellar, and the vault itself refuses a conversion that pays less than its **floor**: the USDC at the Reflector oracle's XLM and USDC prices, less the VaultFactory's discount (its code caps it at 10 %), using a price at most a few minutes old. The XLM amount is known once the conversion has run: the settlement's `delivery`. There is no quote: to show an estimate beforehand, multiply the USDC that would arrive (see *Fees*) by an XLM price of your own; the conversion runs minutes later at that moment's price, so any estimate is approximate.
- **Recipients.** A G, M or C address. A G account that does not exist yet is created by the XLM payment. A **C (contract)** recipient receives the XLM in its own balance, so it must be a contract that can use XLM and can authorize the vault's `withdraw`, as a smart wallet that implements `__check_auth` does. Check that before you create the address, because the protocol cannot: XLM paid to a contract that cannot move it (a token or pool contract, for example) is lost, and the USDC in the vault of a contract that cannot authorize `withdraw` can only leave it through our conversion.
- **Minimum.** The chain's `min_settlement_amount` applies, as for USDC. The USDC that arrives, after fees, must also convert to at least the vault's minimum delivery (2 XLM), which any balance above the minimum does unless XLM trades far above a dollar; should it not, the settlement waits in the vault, `held` with `conversion_unavailable`, until the price allows or the recipient withdraws.
- **Withdraw.** Until the conversion runs, the recipient can take the USDC back out of the vault themselves: they call `withdraw(owner, factory, token)` on their vault (its address follows from theirs: see *Verifying an address*), with `owner` their own address as bytes (its ASCII), `factory` the `xlm_delivery.vault_factory` and `token` Stellar's USDC asset contract, and authorize it. A G or M recipient's account must exist and hold a USDC trustline; a C recipient authorizes it itself. The settlement then completes with the USDC as its `delivery` and the withdraw as its `destination_tx`.
- **Availability.** A new XLM address needs XLM delivery offered: deployed in this environment and switched on (`delivery_asset_unavailable` otherwise). `xlm_delivery.status` says whether conversions run now. While it is `suspended`, XLM addresses keep working: USDC sent to them waits, safely, until conversions run again.

**Advice for integrators**

- **What it is for.** XLM delivery is send-and-forget: no quote is locked, and the conversion runs minutes after the deposit (Circle's finality wait, then about `xlm_delivery.additional_delivery_seconds`), at the venue's price of that moment. That makes it the way to activate an account or top up a balance. A user who wants a precise amount of XLM, or a large one, is better served by USDC delivery and a swap in your wallet, where they see a live quote and set their own slippage. In an onboarding flow, preset amounts (10, 20, 50, 100 USDC) work better than a free-form field. Anyone holding the address can still send any amount to it, and that is fine: see *size* below.
- **Cost and size.** The venue's cost is its pool fee plus price impact, which grows with the amount: about 0.1 % for a few hundred USDC, 0.4 % for 10,000 and 1 % for 30,000 as measured at launch; that is the pool's depth, not a setting of ours. An estimate from a spot price does not include price impact, so a large amount converts for a little less, never for less than the floor at the time. There is no maximum: an amount the venue cannot fill within the floor waits, `held` with `conversion_unavailable`, re-checked every few minutes until it can, or until the recipient withdraws the USDC.
- **What to show.** Show an approximate XLM amount from your own price source, say that the user receives at least the oracle price less the discount at the time of the conversion, and show the settlement's `delivery` once it is there. While a settlement is `held` with `conversion_unavailable`, the USDC is safe: the user can wait, or withdraw it.
- **On testnet.** The discount is set to its 10 % cap and we keep the venue's pool priced ourselves, because nobody else does: the prices and floors you see here say nothing about mainnet.

### Transfer speeds
Circle's CCTP moves USDC at two speeds. **Standard** waits for the source chain's finality (about 15 to 20 minutes from Ethereum) and has no CCTP fee today. **Fast** is attested by Circle seconds after the settlement transaction, for a fee that Circle takes from the amount delivered on Stellar.

- **Chosen per address.** Pass `speed` (`"standard"` or `"fast"`) when you create the address. The speed is part of the address and never changes. A recipient can have one address per delivery asset and speed in your app; each has its own `index`, `setup_fee` and settlements.
- **Offered per chain.** `speeds` in `GET /v1/chains` says, for each chain and speed, whether it is `available`, Circle's maximum fee and the usual delivery time. A fast address settles fast where `speeds.fast.available` is true. Everywhere else it settles at standard speed, with no fast fee: Polygon, whose standard transfers already take a few minutes, does not offer fast. You can create a new fast address only while at least one chain offers fast (`speed_unavailable` otherwise); an existing one keeps working either way.
- **Best effort.** Fast is a request to Circle. If Circle cannot serve it (for example, its fee rose above our maximum), the settlement is delivered at standard speed. A settlement's `executed_speed` says how it was actually delivered.
- **Fee.** Circle's fee is a rate of the burned amount (`settled_amount` minus our fees), at most the speed's `max_cctp_fee_ppm`. What it actually charged is in the settlement's `fees.cctp_fee`.
- **Self-rescue** always settles at standard speed, with no fee.

### Verifying an address
Before you show a deposit address, compute it yourself and compare it with `deposit_address`. Pin the factory and implementation addresses in your own release instead of taking them from the response you are checking. You can find them in `GET /v1/chains` under the top-level `contracts`: one set for every chain of an environment. The contracts are immutable (there is no upgrade mechanism) and we will not replace them, so an issued address stays valid permanently and pinned values never go stale.

There are two ways to compute it:

- **On-chain:** call the factory's read-only `computeAddress(bytes recipient, uint256 index, bool fast)` with `recipient` as the UTF-8 bytes of the address string, `index` from the response, and `fast` true exactly when the response's `speed` is `fast`. The result must equal `deposit_address`.
- **Offline:** use our SDK, [`@lightsail-network/crossmesh-ingress-verify-sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lightsail-network/crossmesh-ingress-verify-sdk) (source in the [contracts repository](https://github.com/lightsail-network/crossmesh-ingress-contracts/tree/main/verify-sdk)). It pins the contracts of both environments and also validates the recipient: `verifyDepositAddress({ depositAddress, recipient, deliveryAsset, speed, index, network })` returns whether they match. Take `depositAddress` and `index` from the response and the rest from your request, `recipient` from your own record of the user: an address bound to someone else's recipient verifies against that recipient. Version 2 is published under the `dev` tag for now (`npm install @lightsail-network/crossmesh-ingress-verify-sdk@dev`); version 1 takes `fast` instead of `speed` and has no `deliveryAsset`.

Test vector on testnet (factory `0xAD93f57DeA4F6bE812c0e1790dF5D3d1161BEd09`, implementation `0xb0216D95AFf228EB8b3A53C58f780D115eFfEC0F`): recipient `GBRAD6AQVETCVZDBT3TLU3KXGPQIXOIQX5DLJYKHNZ4ZF6AWYQXEZGQD` with index `0` gives `0x93845A25A3a5F9b15c25532797CE56fD4851Fcce` at standard speed and `0x36b10Bac9dfb4C10947dCd49cB480594F0a1124B` at fast speed.

An XLM address commits the recipient's vault instead of the recipient, so it is checked in two steps: derive the vault from the recipient, then the address from the vault as above, with the vault's address string as `recipient`. The vault is the contract address the Stellar protocol gives the VaultFactory (`xlm_delivery.vault_factory`) with the salt `sha256(the recipient's address as ASCII)` on this network (contracts repository, `stellar/docs/DESIGN.md` §4). The factory's read-only `vault_address(recipient bytes)` returns it on-chain, and the SDK's `computeVaultAddress({ recipient, network })` offline; `verifyDepositAddress` with `deliveryAsset: "XLM"` checks both steps. Pin `xlm_delivery.vault_factory` as you pin the EVM contracts; the vault code it deploys is fixed in its on-chain configuration and published in the contracts repository.

XLM test vector on testnet: recipient `GBRAD6AQVETCVZDBT3TLU3KXGPQIXOIQX5DLJYKHNZ4ZF6AWYQXEZGQD` has the vault `CDA3QZIJCC3A24IYQNZF3ZAUHETPTDMD3MLPDDR3YHZI6PUBZYO6ICP6`, whose address at index `0` is `0xa0A2039c46e7Bbf45488B916d13F19e74a48143a` at standard speed and `0xCAbff116dFfEb86319DaFBB25Fcfc352E2062C6E` at fast speed.

### What to send
- **Only the chain's USDC:** the token at `usdc_address` in `GET /v1/chains`. On Polygon that is Circle's native USDC, not the bridged USDC.e. Any other token, or the chain's native coin, is not bridged and does not appear in this API. We can recover it only by a manual rescue, which sends it to us; contact support.
- **Only on chains listed as `active`.** The address exists on every EVM chain, but USDC sent on a chain we do not list cannot be moved until we add that chain, and we can add only a chain where Circle's CCTP supports USDC: on any other chain that USDC is lost. If it happens on a chain with CCTP, contact support. USDC sent on a listed chain while it is `suspended` is safe and is processed when the chain is active again.
- **Any amount.** A balance below the chain's `min_settlement_amount` waits for more deposits to the same address on the same chain (`held` with `below_minimum`). There is no maximum: a balance above Circle's per-message CCTP limit (10,000,000 USDC today) is delivered in several rounds, each its own settlement with its own `base_fee` (see `continuation_of`).
- **To a recipient that can hold USDC.** With USDC delivery, a G or M account must exist and have a USDC trustline. Until then its deposits are `held` with `recipient_not_ready`, and they continue automatically once it does. A C (contract) address needs neither, and neither does a recipient of XLM delivery.

### Statuses
A deposit's `status`:

| status | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `confirmed` | Recorded, not yet part of a settlement. Usually seconds; up to a couple of minutes while an earlier settlement of the same address is being sent. |
| `settling` | Its settlement is in progress: the EVM transaction, Circle's attestation, then delivery on Stellar. |
| `held` | Its settlement is waiting for something. `hold_reason` says what. |
| `completed` | Delivered on Stellar. |

A settlement uses the same values except `confirmed`, and every deposit in a settlement shows the settlement's status.

`hold_reason` is set only while the status is `held`:

| hold_reason | meaning | what to tell the user |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `below_minimum` | The address's unsettled balance on this chain is below `min_settlement_amount`, or too small to cover the fees. Nothing is lost: the next deposit to the same address on the same chain that brings the balance to the minimum settles the whole balance, this deposit included. | Send at least the missing amount to the same address on the same chain (the minimum minus the total of the held deposits there); all of it is then delivered together. |
| `recipient_not_ready` | The Stellar account does not exist or has no USDC trustline. | Add a USDC trustline. |
| `chain_unavailable` | The chain is `suspended` in `GET /v1/chains`: we paused it, or its contracts or Circle's CCTP fail our live check. It continues once the chain is active again. | Processing. |
| `gas_too_high` | Gas on the chain is above our limit. We wait for it to fall. | Processing. |
| `operator_not_allowed`, `reorg_check` | An operational issue on our side. We are alerted. | Processing. |
| `external_settlement_unverified` | Someone other than us settled the address, and we could not match that transaction to this deposit. We check the delivery by hand. | Contact support. |
| `conversion_unavailable` | XLM delivery: the conversion cannot run right now, because XLM delivery is paused, the oracle price is stale, no route pays the floor, or the amount would convert to less than the minimum delivery of 2 XLM. The USDC waits in the recipient's vault (or, before it is sent, at the deposit address). | Processing. The recipient may also withdraw the USDC from the vault. |

Holds are re-checked automatically and clear once their cause is gone: `below_minimum` the moment another deposit reaches the address, `recipient_not_ready` every few minutes at first and at least every 30 minutes after that, `chain_unavailable`, `gas_too_high` and `conversion_unavailable` every few minutes. `operator_not_allowed` and `reorg_check` need us, and we are alerted; `external_settlement_unverified` is checked by hand. Funds are never lost in any status, because a deposit address can only settle to its recipient.

### Timing
A deposit appears here about 30 s after its block is `confirmations` deep on its chain (see `GET /v1/chains`): Ethereum makes a block every 12 s, Polygon every 2 s or so. Delivery then usually takes the chain's `estimated_delivery_seconds` for the address's speed: `speeds.fast` for a fast address where fast is available, `speeds.standard` otherwise. At standard speed that is mostly Circle's finality wait: about 15 to 20 minutes on Ethereum and a few minutes on Polygon. Fast from Ethereum takes about a minute. XLM delivery adds the conversion, about `xlm_delivery.additional_delivery_seconds`. If a chain's RPC or Circle has an outage, deposits are delayed, not lost: we pick them up once it recovers.

### Fees
Two kinds of fee come out of a settlement: ours, and Circle's CCTP fee. `GET /v1/chains` publishes both per chain, ours under `fees` and Circle's maximum per speed under `speeds`:

- `setup_fee`: ours, once per deposit address per chain, on its first settlement on that chain.
- `base_fee`: ours, on every settlement.
- `fee_rate_ppm`: ours, a proportional fee in parts per million of the settled amount (a rate: do not scale it by `decimals`). It is 0 today.
- `max_cctp_fee_ppm`: the most Circle's CCTP fee can be at that speed, in parts per million of what is burned (the settled amount minus our fees). Circle takes its fee on Stellar from the minted amount: 0 at standard speed today, and at fast speed its current fast fee (1 bps from Ethereum at the time of writing).

Each settlement reports what it paid under `fees` (`setup_fee`, `settlement_fee`, `cctp_fee`) and the USDC that arrived on Stellar as `minted_amount`:

```
setup_fee        = the chain's setup_fee on the address's first settlement there, otherwise 0
settlement_fee   = base_fee + floor(settled_amount × fee_rate_ppm ÷ 1,000,000)
cctp_fee         ≤ ceil((settled_amount − setup_fee − settlement_fee) × max_cctp_fee_ppm ÷ 1,000,000)
minted_amount    = settled_amount − setup_fee − settlement_fee − cctp_fee
```

`max_cctp_fee_ppm` is that of the speed the settlement was delivered at, its `executed_speed`. A depositor's own sweep (`via_sweep`) pays none of our fees. With USDC delivery the recipient receives exactly `minted_amount`, which the settlement's `delivery` reports once delivered; with XLM delivery `minted_amount` is converted to XLM at no less than the floor (see *XLM delivery*). For example, a fast settlement of 20 USDC that pays no setup fee, on a chain whose `base_fee` is 0.5 USDC, while Circle's fast fee is 1 bps: `settlement_fee` = 500000, `cctp_fee` = 1950 (1 bps of the 19500000 burned), `minted_amount` = 19498050, so the recipient receives 19.49805 USDC.

All values are in USDC base units. Our proportional part is rounded down to a whole base unit, as the contract does, and Circle's maximum is rounded up. The values in `GET /v1/chains` are read live from the on-chain Config and limited by immutable on-chain caps you can verify, so read them before quoting a fee.

### Polling
There are no webhooks. Choose by what you need:

- **To show one user's deposits,** read `GET /v1/deposits?recipient=<address>` each time you show them. One recipient's list is short, so read it whole; there is nothing to track.
- **To follow every change in your backend** (for example, to notify users), poll `GET /v1/deposits?updated_after=<the largest updated_at you hold>`, and `GET /v1/settlements` the same way. How often is up to you: we record new deposits about every 30 s, so polling much more often gains little. With `updated_after` the results come oldest change first: follow `next_cursor` until `has_more` is false, and the last row's `updated_at` is the value for your next poll. A row that changes while you page moves to the end, so you get it later in the same read or in your next poll. Any change to a deposit's status, hold or settlement updates its `updated_at`. The value has millisecond precision and comes from a single clock, so passing it back unchanged returns only later changes.

There is no hard rate limit today. Keep to a few requests per second per key.

### Self-rescue
If we ever stop settling, anyone can move a deposit address's USDC to its recipient, without us and without fees. Every step is a permissionless call, and the funds can still only go to the committed recipient.

1. If the address has never been settled on that chain, deploy its forwarder with the factory's `deploy(recipientBytes, index, fast)`, with `fast` true exactly when the address's `speed` is `fast`. With the other value you deploy a different address.
2. Call `requestSweep()` on the deposit address, wait the Config's `sweepDelay` (24 hours on mainnet and 1 hour on testnet today, at most 7 days by contract), then call `sweep()`. A sweep always uses standard speed.
3. Deliver the burn on Stellar: fetch Circle's attestation for the sweep transaction and submit `mint_and_forward` to Stellar's CCTP forwarder. Anyone can do this. While we operate, we deliver such sweeps ourselves (`via_sweep` on the settlement).
4. With XLM delivery the USDC arrives in the recipient's vault, from which the recipient withdraws it (see *XLM delivery*). Anyone can deploy the vault first, through the VaultFactory's permissionless `deploy(recipient bytes)`.

### Environments
There are two separate deployments, each with its own accounts, API keys and deposit addresses:

- **mainnet:** Ethereum and Polygon to Stellar mainnet. Console accounts are by invitation.
- **testnet:** Ethereum Sepolia and Polygon Amoy to Stellar testnet, using Circle's testnet USDC. Registration is open.

This reference is served by the **testnet** deployment. Chain identifiers (`ethereum`, `polygon`) are the same on both, so the same code works against either. The contracts, `chain_id` values and addresses differ.

### Pagination
List endpoints return the newest rows first. Pass `limit`, and `starting_after` set to the previous page's `next_cursor`. `has_more` tells you whether more rows remain.

### Errors
Every non-2xx response is `{ error: { code, message, request_id } }` with the matching HTTP status. `code` is stable and machine-readable, so branch on it. `message` is for humans and may change. Include `request_id` when you contact support.

| code | HTTP | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | 400 | A parameter or body field failed validation, including a bad `starting_after` cursor or date. |
| `request_failed` | 4xx | The request could not be processed, for example malformed JSON, an unsupported content type or an oversized body. |
| `invalid_stellar_address` | 400 | `recipient` is not a valid Stellar G, M or C address, or is one of the network's own contracts (Circle's CCTP forwarder, the USDC or XLM asset contract, XLM delivery's VaultFactory or filler). |
| `authentication_failed` | 401 | The API key is missing, malformed or revoked, or the key's app or account is suspended. |
| `deposit_not_found` · `deposit_address_not_found` · `settlement_not_found` · `not_found` | 404 | No such resource under your app, or no such route. |
| `delivery_asset_unavailable` | 400 | A new address for a `delivery_asset` this environment does not offer right now: `XLM` where XLM delivery is not deployed or is switched off. An address you already have is always returned. |
| `speed_unavailable` | 400 | `speed: "fast"` for a new address while no chain offers fast transfers (see `speeds.fast` in `GET /v1/chains`). An existing fast address is always returned. |
| `address_limit_reached` | 409 | Your app has reached its deposit address limit. Only a first call for a new address can hit it. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | A server fault. Safe to retry; contact support with the `request_id` if it persists. |

### Support
Your users contact you, and we support you: for what you cannot resolve from the API, reach us on the Cross Mesh **Discord** (the invite comes with your API access). If your product names Cross Mesh as the provider of this feature, your users can also reach us there directly. Send the `deposit_id` or `settlement_id` (or the EVM `source_tx` hash), and for an error response its `request_id`. Contact us for a deposit `held` with `external_settlement_unverified`, or one held for more than about an hour for any reason other than `below_minimum` or `recipient_not_ready`.

### Versioning
The version is in the path (`/v1`). Within it we only add: endpoints, optional parameters, response fields, and values of enumerations such as `status`, `hold_reason`, `delivery_asset` and error `code`. Build for that: ignore fields you do not know, show a `status` or `hold_reason` you do not know as processing, and handle an error `code` you do not know by its HTTP status. A change that would break an integration built this way, such as removing or renaming a field or changing its meaning, ships under a new prefix.

get.summary: Describe this environment: source chains, contracts, XLM delivery
get.description:
Everything your deposit screen needs about this environment, in one call. `chains` lists the source chains we support: each with its EIP-155 `chain_id`, its USDC contract, the current `fees`, the `min_settlement_amount`, the `confirmations` we wait before recording a deposit, and its `speeds`: whether each transfer speed is available there, Circle's maximum fee and a typical `estimated_delivery_seconds`. `contracts` are the EVM contracts to pin for verifying addresses (the same on every chain). `xlm_delivery` says whether XLM delivery is offered here and runs now, names the VaultFactory to pin for verifying XLM addresses, and gives the time a conversion adds (see *XLM delivery*); it is null where XLM delivery is not deployed.

Fees, minimums and availability change, and a chain or XLM delivery can be paused: read this before quoting a fee, a minimum or a delivery time, and cache it for a minute at most. Public: authentication is optional.

200.description: This environment: the EVM contracts to pin, XLM delivery, and the supported source chains.

contracts.description: Our contracts, for independent verification: the same addresses on every chain of this environment, which is why a deposit address (computed from the factory and implementation) is the same on every chain too. Null only before any chain is configured.

config.description: Config contract (EIP-55). Each chain's instance holds that chain's fees (each chain's `fees`), their caps and the operator; read them on-chain to verify.

forwarder_implementation.description: Forwarder implementation (EIP-55). Together with the factory, it determines every deposit address.

factory.description: Factory (EIP-55). Deploys forwarders; its computeAddress returns any deposit address on-chain.

xlm_delivery.description: XLM delivery in this environment (see *XLM delivery*). Offer the user XLM delivery only when this is not null; its status says whether conversions run right now. Null where XLM delivery is not deployed.

status.description: Whether conversions run now. "active": deposits to XLM addresses are converted and delivered. "suspended": XLM delivery is paused, or its contracts fail our live check: no conversion runs, and USDC sent to an XLM address waits safely (at the deposit address, or in the recipient's vault once minted) until it is active again. Show XLM as delayed, not unavailable: existing XLM addresses keep working either way. Only while XLM delivery is paused is a new XLM address refused (delivery_asset_unavailable).

vault_factory.description: The VaultFactory, a Stellar contract (C…): every recipient's vault, and so every XLM deposit address, is derived from it. You do not need it to create or use addresses; pin it, as you pin the EVM `contracts`, to verify XLM addresses yourself (see *Verifying an address*). It never changes within an environment.

additional_delivery_seconds.description: Typical seconds the conversion adds after the USDC reaches Stellar. For an XLM address, add it to the chain's estimated_delivery_seconds. An estimate.

chain.description: Chain identifier, e.g. "ethereum" or "polygon". Use it wherever this API refers to a chain. It is the same on mainnet and testnet; chain_id tells them apart.

chain_id.description: EIP-155 chain id on this environment, e.g. 1 for Ethereum mainnet or 11155111 for Sepolia. The user's wallet must be on this chain when sending.

status.description: "active": accepting deposits. "suspended": temporarily not accepting deposits, because we paused it or our live check of the chain's contracts or Circle's CCTP is failing. Do not send on a suspended chain; USDC already sent there is safe and is processed when the chain is active again. A chain that is not listed is not supported: the deposit address exists there too, but USDC sent on it cannot be moved until we add that chain, which is possible only where Circle's CCTP supports USDC (elsewhere it is lost).

usdc_address.description: The USDC token contract on this chain (Circle's native USDC, EIP-55 checksummed). Only transfers of this token are detected and bridged. Any other token (including bridged USDC.e on Polygon) or the chain's native coin is not, and can only be recovered by a manual rescue on our side.

confirmations.description: How many blocks we wait after a USDC transfer's block before recording it as a deposit. It appears in GET /v1/deposits about 30 s later. Because we wait this long, a chain reorganization cannot undo a deposit we have shown you.

min_settlement_amount.description: Smallest deposit address balance that settles on this chain, in USDC base units (6 decimals). It applies to the balance, not to each transfer: a deposit that leaves the balance below it is held as below_minimum and settles together with the next deposit that brings the balance to it or above.

decimals.description: Decimal places of min_settlement_amount (always 6 for USDC). Human value = amount / 10^decimals.

available.description: Whether settlements at this speed run on this chain now: the chain is active.

max_cctp_fee_ppm.description: The most Circle can take from a settlement at this speed here, in parts per million of the burned amount (settled minus our fees), rounded up to a whole base unit. It is the on-chain allowance, which you can verify on the chain's Config. "0" = free. A rate, not an amount: do not scale it by decimals. Null when not available.

estimated_delivery_seconds.description: Typical seconds from a deposit appearing in this API to its delivery on Stellar at this speed. An estimate, not a guarantee: high gas, congestion or a missing trustline can delay it. Null when not available.

available.description: Whether settlements at this speed run on this chain now: the chain is active and offers fast transfers (we offer them there, and its Config has them enabled).

max_cctp_fee_ppm.description: The most Circle can take from a settlement at this speed here, in parts per million of the burned amount (settled minus our fees), rounded up to a whole base unit. It is the on-chain allowance, which you can verify on the chain's Config. "0" = free. A rate, not an amount: do not scale it by decimals. Null when not available.

estimated_delivery_seconds.description: Typical seconds from a deposit appearing in this API to its delivery on Stellar at this speed. An estimate, not a guarantee: high gas, congestion or a missing trustline can delay it. Null when not available.

speeds.description: Each transfer speed on this chain (see *Transfer speeds*), read live from the chain's Config. A deposit address settles at its own `speed` where that speed is `available`, and at standard speed where it is not.

fees.description: The fees Cross Mesh charges per settlement, read live from the on-chain Config and limited by immutable on-chain caps. They are the same at both speeds. A settlement pays setup_fee (on an address's first settlement on this chain only) and base_fee + settled_amount × fee_rate_ppm ÷ 1,000,000 (rounded down to a whole base unit), which it reports as `fees.setup_fee` and `fees.settlement_fee`. Circle's CCTP fee comes on top of ours (see `speeds`), and the recipient receives the rest: settled_amount − setup_fee − settlement_fee − cctp_fee. Our fees must be below the settled amount, so a balance too small to cover them is held as below_minimum. Read these values before quoting a fee. Null only when a chain is not active and its fees could not be read.

setup_fee.description: Charged once per deposit address per chain, on its first settlement on that chain. USDC base units.

base_fee.description: Charged on every settlement. USDC base units.

fee_rate_ppm.description: Proportional fee in parts per million of the settled amount, e.g. "100" = 0.01%. A rate, not an amount: do not scale it by decimals. It is 0 today and may be enabled later.

decimals.description: Decimal places of setup_fee and base_fee (always 6 for USDC). fee_rate_ppm is a rate and takes none.

post.summary: Get or create the deposit address for a recipient
post.description:
Return the EVM deposit address bound to a Stellar recipient for a delivery asset and a transfer speed, creating it on the first call. In your app each recipient has exactly one address per delivery asset and speed, permanently: every later call with the same `delivery_asset` and `speed`, before or after any number of deposits, returns the same address. So it is safe to call each time you display the address, and safe to retry.

The address works on every chain in GET /v1/chains and receives all of the recipient's deposits. A fast address settles fast where a chain's `speeds.fast` is available and at standard speed elsewhere (see *Transfer speeds*). Its one-time `setup_fee` is paid once per chain, on the first settlement there. With USDC delivery, a G or M recipient must exist and have a USDC trustline to receive; until then its deposits are `held` with `recipient_not_ready` and continue automatically. A C (contract) recipient needs neither. With XLM delivery the address commits the recipient's vault and the recipient needs neither: the XLM creates a G account that does not exist yet (see *XLM delivery*). Check the returned address before you show it (see *Verifying an address*).

Errors: 400 `invalid_stellar_address` for a bad recipient; 400 `delivery_asset_unavailable` for a new XLM address where XLM delivery is not offered; 400 `speed_unavailable` for a new fast address while no chain offers fast; 409 `address_limit_reached` when a new address would exceed your app's address limit. An address you already have is always returned.

recipient.description: Stellar address to bind the deposit address to: a G (account), M (muxed account) or C (contract) address. Everything sent to the returned address is delivered here. For XLM delivery, a C recipient must be able to use XLM and to authorize its vault's `withdraw` (see *XLM delivery*).

delivery_asset.description: What the recipient receives. Required: `USDC`, or `XLM` where XLM delivery is offered (see *XLM delivery*; otherwise 400 `delivery_asset_unavailable`). Like the speed, it is part of the address and cannot be changed later.

speed.description: Transfer speed of the address. Required: `standard` or `fast` (see *Transfer speeds*). It is part of the address and cannot be changed later; a recipient can have one address per delivery asset and speed.

200.description: The deposit address bound to the recipient.

deposit_address.description: EVM address to send USDC to (EIP-55 checksummed). It is this recipient's one address in your app for this delivery asset and speed and receives all of its deposits, so reuse it. Case-insensitive wherever you pass it back.

recipient.description: Stellar recipient (G…, M… or C…) permanently bound to this address. Everything sent here is delivered to it.

delivery_asset.description: What this address delivers to its recipient, fixed when it was created: `USDC`, or `XLM` (see *XLM delivery*).

speed.description: The address's transfer speed (see *Transfer speeds*). Fixed when the address was created: it is part of the address. When you verify the address, pass `fast` = (speed is `fast`).

index.description: Address index for what the address commits: the recipient, or its vault for XLM delivery. Indices are unique per committed recipient across all integrators, so yours may not start at 0, and a recipient's standard and fast addresses have different ones. Together with recipient, delivery_asset, speed and the contracts, it determines deposit_address: check it before showing the address (see *Verifying an address* at the top of this reference).

created_at.description: When the address was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

status.description: confirmed (recorded, not yet in a settlement), then settling (being delivered), then completed (delivered on Stellar). held means its settlement is waiting; see hold_reason. Details under *Statuses* at the top of this reference. One rare exception to completed being final: a deposit that we record late, ahead of a balance above Circle's per-message limit, can move from a delivered round to the next one, because rounds take deposits in chain order.

Show the others as processing; with conversion_unavailable the USDC waits at the deposit address, or in the user's vault once minted, where the user may also withdraw it. external_settlement_unverified is resolved by hand: contact support. status.description: settling (being delivered: the EVM transaction, Circle's attestation, the Stellar delivery, and for XLM delivery the conversion), then completed (delivered on Stellar: with XLM delivery, converted to XLM, or withdrawn as USDC by the recipient before the conversion, which delivery reports). held means it is waiting; see hold_reason. Every deposit in the settlement shows this same status.

The user can act on below_minimum (send the missing amount to the same address on the same chain) and recipient_not_ready (create the account or add a USDC trustline). Show the others as processing; with conversion_unavailable the USDC waits at the deposit address, or in the user's vault once minted, where the user may also withdraw it. external_settlement_unverified is resolved by hand: contact support. Each value is explained under *Statuses* at the top of this reference.

deposit_address.description: The EVM deposit address this settlement moves USDC from (EIP-55 checksummed).

recipient.description: Stellar recipient (G…, M… or C…) the settlement is delivered to.

delivery_asset.description: What its deposit address delivers (that address's delivery_asset): `USDC` or `XLM`.

deposit_count.description: How many deposits this settlement delivers; list them with GET /v1/deposits?settlement_id=…. A settlement carries exactly the deposits that reached the address after the previous settlement transaction and before its own, so you can check the count on-chain. Only for a balance above Circle's per-message limit does this differ: a round carries part of the balance, deposits are assigned oldest first, and a deposit split across two rounds counts in the round that delivers its last part.

settled_amount.description: USDC that left the deposit address in this settlement: the sum of its deposits, or less for one round of a balance above Circle's per-message limit. Null until the settlement transaction is recorded. USDC base units (6 decimals).

fees.description: The fees actually charged, as recorded on-chain, in USDC base units. Null until the settlement transaction is recorded.

setup_fee.description: Setup fee charged in this settlement. Non-zero only on the address's first settlement on this chain.

settlement_fee.description: Per-settlement fee charged: base_fee + settled_amount × fee_rate_ppm ÷ 1,000,000, the proportional part rounded down (see GET /v1/chains). The contract records the two parts as one amount. 0 when the depositor settled the address themselves (via_sweep).

cctp_fee.description: Circle's CCTP fee, taken on Stellar from the minted amount: 0 for a standard transfer, Circle's fast fee when executed_speed is fast. Null until Circle attests.

decimals.description: Decimal places of the fee amounts (6 for USDC).

minted_amount.description: USDC that arrived on Stellar: settled_amount − setup_fee − settlement_fee − cctp_fee (see *Fees*). With USDC delivery it is what the recipient receives; with XLM delivery it is what is converted to XLM. Null until Circle attests. USDC base units (6 decimals).

decimals.description: Decimal places of settled_amount and minted_amount (6 for USDC). Stellar shows USDC with 7 decimals; the value is the same. delivery carries its own decimals.

delivery.description: What the recipient received on Stellar, as one credit in destination_tx. This is the amount to show the user. With USDC delivery it equals minted_amount; with XLM delivery it is the XLM the conversion paid, known only once it ran, or minted_amount in USDC when the recipient withdrew it from their vault before the conversion (then asset is USDC on an XLM address, and destination_tx is their withdraw). Null until then; it also stays null on the rare completed settlement whose amounts are unknown (see external_settlement_unverified).

asset.description: The asset the recipient received: `USDC`, or `XLM` (XLM delivery, unless the recipient withdrew the USDC).

amount.description: The amount received, in base units of that asset.

decimals.description: Decimal places of amount: 6 for USDC, 7 for XLM.

executed_speed.description: How Circle actually delivered this settlement (see *Transfer speeds*). A fast address's settlement can be `standard`: on a chain where fast is not available, for the depositor's own sweep, or when Circle could not serve fast. Set when Circle attests, which is before the Stellar delivery; null until then.

via_sweep.description: true when the EVM transaction was the depositor's own fee-free sweep (see *Self-rescue*), which we then delivered on Stellar, rather than our settlement. false until a settlement transaction is recorded.

continuation_of.description: Set on a later round of a balance above Circle's per-message limit (see *What to send*): the settlement_id of the round before it.

source_tx.description: Hash of the EVM settlement transaction (ours, or the depositor's sweep). It burns the USDC through Circle's CCTP: the burn that cctp_mint_tx completes on Stellar. Null until it is recorded.

cctp_mint_tx.description: Stellar transaction hash of Circle's CCTP mint (the claim) that brought minted_amount to Stellar: to the recipient, or into its vault with XLM delivery. With USDC delivery it is also destination_tx. Null until minted, and in rare cases after: when an outside relayer minted first and we could not recover the hash.

destination_tx.description: Stellar transaction hash of the delivery that delivery reports: the CCTP mint (USDC delivery), the conversion to XLM, or the recipient's own withdraw of the USDC before the conversion. Use status to tell whether it was delivered: in rare cases this stays null after a USDC delivery, when an outside relayer delivered first.

created_at.description: When the settlement was opened (ISO 8601, UTC).

updated_at.description: When the settlement's status or hold last changed (ISO 8601, UTC, millisecond precision). Use it with updated_after to poll for changes.

items.description: A settlement: one EVM transaction and one Stellar credit, carrying one or more deposits.

data.description: Rows for this page, newest first.

has_more.description: true if more rows exist past this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor: pass it as starting_after to get the next page. Null on the last page.

get.description: Read one settlement: its status, the amount settled on EVM, the fees charged, the amount delivered on Stellar, the speed Circle delivered it at, and the EVM and Stellar transaction hashes. Returns 404 `settlement_not_found` if it is not one of your app's settlements.

status.description: settling (being delivered: the EVM transaction, Circle's attestation, the Stellar delivery, and for XLM delivery the conversion), then completed (delivered on Stellar: with XLM delivery, converted to XLM, or withdrawn as USDC by the recipient before the conversion, which delivery reports). held means it is waiting; see hold_reason.
